name: Omega-3-acid ethyl esters
className: Lipid-modifying agent (omega-3 fatty acid ethyl esters, EPA and DHA)

formulations.label: Capsules, soft
formulations.strengths: 1000 mg (840 mg EPA and DHA ethyl esters)
formulations.note: Soya content differs between UK products: two UK SmPCs list soya hypersensitivity as a contraindication (soya oil in the antioxidant); another UK SmPC does not list soya.

src.q: comprising 840 mg eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) ethyl ester (460mg) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) ethyl ester (380mg)

items.t: Endogenous hypertriglyceridaemia, as a supplement to diet when diet alone is not enough: type IV alone; type IIb/III with a statin when triglycerides are not controlled. Not for exogenous hypertriglyceridaemia (type 1 hyperchylomicronaemia).

src.q: Endogenous hypertriglyceridaemia as a supplement to diet when dietary measures alone are insufficient to produce an adequate response
type IIb/III in combination with statins, when control of triglycerides is insufficient
Omacor is not indicated in exogenous hypertriglyceridaemia (type 1 hyperchylomicronaemia).

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction or brand-specific prescribing statement in the three UK SmPCs used; the MHRA Drug Safety Update (January 2024) covers atrial fibrillation risk only. No SPS advice found.

items.t: Start with 2 capsules (2 g) daily; if response is not adequate, increase to 4 capsules (4 g) daily.

src.q: Initial treatment two capsules daily. If adequate response is not obtained, the dose may be increased to four capsules daily.

items.t: Limited data in people over 70 years and in renal impairment; no information in hepatic impairment.

src.q: There is limited clinical data regarding the use of Omacor in elderly patients over 70 years of age and patients with renal impairment

items.t: Not recommended in children (no efficacy or safety data).

src.q: In the absence of efficacy and safety data, use of this medication in children is not recommended.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or any excipient. Two UK SmPCs also list soya; one says do not use if allergic to peanut or soya (contains soya oil).

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance, to soya or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
If you are allergic to peanut or soya, do not use this medicinal product.

items.t: Dose-dependent increased risk of atrial fibrillation in patients with cardiovascular disease or risk factors, highest at 4 g/day. If atrial fibrillation develops, stop permanently.

src.q: The observed risk is highest with a dose of 4 g/daily (see section 4.8). If atrial fibrillation develops, treatment should be permanently discontinued.
if a patient develops atrial fibrillation whilst taking these medicines for the treatment of hypertriglyceridaemia then the medicine should be discontinued permanently

items.t: Bleeding time rises moderately at 4 capsules daily: monitor patients on anticoagulants and adjust the anticoagulant dose if needed; allow for this in patients at high bleeding risk (severe trauma, surgery).

src.q: patients receiving anticoagulant therapy must be monitored and the dosage of anticoagulant adjusted if necessary
Make allowance for the increased bleeding time in patients at high risk of haemorrhage (because of severe trauma, surgery, etc).

items.t: Use with caution in known fish sensitivity or allergy.

src.q: Omacor should be used with caution in patients with known sensitivity or allergy to fish.

items.t: Monitor ALT and AST if there are signs of liver damage (especially at 4 capsules daily). No experience with fibrates; limited experience in secondary hypertriglyceridaemia (e.g. uncontrolled diabetes).

src.q: ALAT and ASAT levels should be monitored in patients with any signs of liver damage (in particular with the high dosage, i.e. 4 capsules).
There is no experience regarding hypertriglyceridaemia in combination with fibrates.

items.t: Warfarin / oral anticoagulants: given together without bleeding complications, but prothrombin time must be checked when combined and when omega-3 is stopped; at 4 capsules daily monitor and adjust the anticoagulant dose if needed.

src.q: the prothrombin time must be checked when Omacor is combined with warfarin or when treatment with Omacor is stopped
patients receiving anticoagulant therapy must be monitored and the dosage of anticoagulant adjusted if necessary

items.t: Only limited information in renal impairment; no threshold or dose adjustment given.

src.q: Only limited information regarding the use in patients with renal impairment is available.

items.t: No information in hepatic impairment; no data showing increased risk. Monitor ALT/AST if there are signs of liver damage.

src.q: there are no data indicating an increased risk for patients with hepatic impairment
ALAT and ASAT levels should be monitored in patients with any signs of liver damage

items.t: No adequate human data; animal studies show no reproductive toxicity. Should not be used in pregnancy unless clearly necessary. No BUMPS leaflet found.

src.q: Omacor should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary

items.t: No data on passage into milk. Should not be used during breastfeeding. No SPS breastfeeding page for omega-3 medicines was found.

src.q: Omacor should not be used during lactation.

items.t: No adequate data on fertility.

src.q: There are no adequate data on the effect of Omacor on fertility.

items.t: Common: atrial fibrillation; gastrointestinal disorders (abdominal distension or pain, constipation, diarrhoea, dyspepsia, flatulence, belching, reflux, nausea or vomiting). Uncommon: dizziness, taste change, headache, hypotension, nosebleed, rash, raised blood glucose, gout.

src.q: Cardiac disorders: Common: atrial fibrillation

Gastrointestinal disorders: Common: gastrointestinal disorders (including abdominal distension, abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhoea, dyspepsia, flatulence, eructation, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, nausea or vomiting)
Nervous system disorders: Uncommon: dizziness, dysgeusia, headache

items.t: Atrial fibrillation (common): advise patients to seek medical attention for palpitations, dizziness, breathlessness or tiredness; stop permanently if it develops.

src.q: advise patients taking omega-3-acid ethyl ester medicines for the treatment of hypertriglyceridaemia to seek medical attention if they develop symptoms of atrial fibrillation
talk to your doctor if you experience palpitations, dizziness, shortness of breath and tiredness

items.t: Uncommon: gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Rare: hypersensitivity, liver disorders (raised transaminases).

src.q: Uncommon: gastrointestinal haemorrhage
Rare: liver disorders (including transaminases increased

items.t: May be taken with food to avoid stomach upset.

items.t: Tell the doctor about any heart problems before starting. Report palpitations, dizziness, breathlessness or tiredness (possible atrial fibrillation). Do not stop treatment without talking to the doctor.

src.q: inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are currently experiencing heart problems or have a history of heart problems
do not stop your hypertriglyceridaemia treatment without first discussing this with your doctor
